- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 14-day moving avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true mean of prior 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.17 for 3+ consecutive days), model overestimates downward trend — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive days of high prices — add 1–3% to forecast to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.1), model often fails to capture short-term volatility — increase forecast variance by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
